sentence: For each request, the router picks one deployment from a model group [RCALL-045].

An earlier request's deployment may hold an earlier answer, a cached long prompt, or locked reasoning that only its account can open [AFFINITY-022] [AFFINITY-061] [AFFINITY-087] [AFFINITY-069] [AFFINITY-072].
note: The account half is now cited. AFFINITY-069: 'The encryption boundary of a deployment is (`api_base`, `api_key`)', which the module's terms call 'the pair ... that decides which upstream account can decrypt encrypted reasoning'; AFFINITY-072 keeps reasoning only when 'the origin is one of the targets' ... or ... the origin's boundary equals some target's boundary'. The other two kinds of state stay as before: AFFINITY-022 decodes `previous_response_id` to a deployment id, AFFINITY-087 is the prompt-cache pin.

sentence: When switched on, the router notes the deployment chosen for a caller or chat session, and the one that served a long prompt [AFFINITY-045] [AFFINITY-046] [AFFINITY-091].
Locked reasoning carries its deployment's name inside the request [AFFINITY-164].
These optional filters send the next request back there [AFFINITY-028] [AFFINITY-029] [AFFINITY-061] [AFFINITY-087].
If a caller's deployment is unhealthy or gone, normal routing picks another [AFFINITY-030].
note: Now scoped to the caller pin, which is what AFFINITY-030 covers: the list is 'returned unchanged when ... the pinned deployment is not among the candidates (unhealthy, cooled down or removed ...), so routing falls back to the strategy over all healthy deployments'. The earlier 'the filters step aside', which the encrypted-content filter contradicts (AFFINITY-062, AFFINITY-064), is gone.

sentence: That caller can then lose its place in the prompt cache for up to an hour by default [AFFINITY-198].
note: Reworded from the plural next to the repaired sentence before it. AFFINITY-198: 'after a deployment is removed or stays unhealthy, its callers lose stickiness and prompt-cache reuse for up to the pin TTL (`3600` s by default, [AFFINITY-003])'.

sentence: A follow-up turn can also lose its locked reasoning without any error [AFFINITY-159].
On the router's async selection path, every registered filter takes the candidate list in turn, after the health and cooldown filters [RSELECT-043] [RSELECT-044] [RSELECT-047] [AFFINITY-009].
The deployment-affinity and prompt-cache filters return the list unchanged or narrowed to one deployment [AFFINITY-022] [AFFINITY-029] [AFFINITY-087].
The encrypted-content filter can keep several, and the continuation filter can keep none [AFFINITY-062] [AFFINITY-133].
A pre-call hook claims caller and session pins just before the provider call, and the first writer wins [AFFINITY-041] [AFFINITY-047].
A success callback writes prompt-cache pins after the call, and the last writer wins [AFFINITY-091] [AFFINITY-114].
model group: the public model name a caller asks for, shared by several deployments
deployment: one configured way to reach a model at a provider, with its own address, key and unique id
locked reasoning: reasoning a provider returned in encrypted form, which a later request replays; only a deployment on the same account keeps it
pin: a stored note that names the deployment holding a caller's, a session's or a prompt's state
candidate list: the deployments still in the running when a filter takes its turn, after earlier filters have had theirs
note: Matches AFFINITY-009 (the router passes 'each filter's output to the next') and AFFINITY-177, now cited ('an encrypted-content pin reaches the deployment-affinity filter as an already-narrowed list'). The module's own term agrees: 'the `healthy_deployments` list a filter receives'.

sentence: filter: an optional check that can shrink the candidate list before the strategy picks one
cooldown: a pause during which the router sends a deployment no traffic
asynchronous call: a request made through the router's non-blocking methods, which let the program do other work while it waits
note: The overstated clause 'the pin filters run on this path' is gone; what remains is a plain gloss of an async call. AFFINITY-012 distinguishes 'sync Router methods' from 'async calls' and states which async calls skip the filters, which the synchronous-call row and the At-a-glance row carry.

sentence: routing strategy: the rule that picks one deployment from the candidates that remain
pre-call checks setting: the router setting that lists which optional filters to build
deployment-affinity filter: the one filter per router that reads caller pins, session pins and earlier response ids
caller pin: a pin per caller and group, switched on by the caller-affinity name
session pin: a pin per client session, scoped to the caller when one is known
response continuity: sending a follow-up to the deployment whose earlier response it names
encrypted-content filter: the filter that returns replayed locked reasoning to a deployment able to decrypt it, when a candidate can
note: AFFINITY-061 and AFFINITY-062 are now cited: the origin candidate gets 'a one-element list', else 'every candidate with an equal boundary is returned'. 'When a candidate can' matches the degrade path of AFFINITY-064 when none qualifies. AFFINITY-062 also needs the router to still know the origin and its boundary to resolve (AFFINITY-063, AFFINITY-069); the steps of the 'encrypted' figure state that condition, so the gloss is a fair summary.

sentence: prompt-cache filter: the filter that returns a long prompt to the deployment pinned for its prefix, when that deployment is a candidate
note: AFFINITY-087, now cited: 'when it names a deployment whose `model_info.id` equals the pinned id ... a one-element list with the first such candidate is returned, otherwise the input list is returned unchanged'. 'Long' is the token threshold of AFFINITY-084, now cited. 'Pinned for its prefix' replaces 'that cached its prefix'; the pin is written by the deployment that served it (AFFINITY-091).

sentence: continuation filter: the filter that keeps only deployments able to finish a broken stream, when a request continues one
note: AFFINITY-133, now cited: 'On a continuation, a deployment is kept only when it supports prefill and its own `litellm_params` do not constrain the output'. 'When a request continues one' matches AFFINITY-130 (it filters only when the continuation marker is present).

sentence: per-group switches: a list of filter names for one group that replaces the global caller, session and response switches
order hop: a fallback attempt aimed at the deployments of one order level inside the group
priority group: a routing group that uses the priority strategy, where caller, session and prompt-cache pins step aside
caller key: who is calling: the virtual key's hash, or else the user id with a prefix
metadata bucket: the request field that carries bookkeeping, where the proxy or the calling program puts the caller and session
note: AFFINITY-184, now cited: the module 'relies on the caller of the router (the proxy's auth layer, or the SDK user) to stamp them'. AFFINITY-150 names the buckets (`litellm_metadata`, then `metadata`). The router is no longer said to write caller and session.

sentence: session marker: a per-request lifetime the router stamps to switch session pins on for one request
pin lifetime: how long a caller or session pin lives without renewal, one hour by default
origin marker: a tag on replayed reasoning that names the deployment that produced it
encryption boundary: the provider address and key pair that decides which account can decrypt reasoning
pinned mark: a request flag that tells the router to skip the strategy when one candidate remains
cache breakpoint: a marker in the messages that ends the part a provider may cache
cache minimum: the fewest prompt tokens a model will cache
continuation marker: a private object the router puts on a request only when it continues a broken stream
prefill support: whether a model accepts a partial assistant answer to carry on from
synchronous call: a request made through the router's blocking methods, which wait for the answer; the pin filters never run for it
process-wide filter list: the one list of filters that every router in the process runs
When a known caller repeats a request, caller pins are on, and no earlier check decided: only the pinned deployment stays, if it is still a candidate
When session pins are on, or the session marker is set, and the request has a client session id: the session pin is read before the caller pin
When response continuity is on, the request is not an order hop, and `previous_response_id` names a candidate: that deployment wins before the priority-group, session and caller checks

When the request is an order hop: the deployment-affinity and prompt-cache filters pass the list through; with an integer order and an origin marker, the encrypted-content filter decides among that order's deployments only
When the group is a priority group: caller, session and prompt-cache pins are skipped
When a group has per-group switches: they replace the global caller, session and response switches (an empty list turns all three off), and can only add the encrypted-content filter
When no candidate is the reasoning's origin or shares its boundary: the reasoning is stripped, a warning is logged, and routing goes on
When the prompt has no cache breakpoint, or is below the candidates' lowest cache minimum (`1024` tokens by default): no prompt-cache pin is read
When the call uses a sync router method, or a router strategy with no async selector: no pin filter runs; only the continuation check applies
When a filter raises, for example when the encrypted-content filter is active and `litellm_metadata` cannot take new keys: selection fails and the caller gets the error
For an asynchronous call, the router first drops deployments that are cooling down or, when health filtering applies, unhealthy [RSELECT-043] [RSELECT-142] [RSELECT-044].
note: 'When health filtering applies' no longer equates the filter with health checks being on. RSELECT-142 lists when it is a no-op ('when `enable_health_check_routing` is off, and also when `allowed_fails_policy` is set while `background_health_check_model_groups` is unset'), and the conditional covers both cases. RSELECT-043 orders health before cooldown; RSELECT-044 removes cooled-down ids. RSELECT-045's restore of an all-cooled-down group is an edge case this summary leaves out.

sentence: Each optional filter that is switched on then gets the remaining list in turn [RSELECT-047] [AFFINITY-009].
The routing strategy picks from what is left, unless the encrypted-content filter left one pinned deployment [RSELECT-068] [AFFINITY-013].
A filter error fails the request, and the caller gets it [AFFINITY-157].
In the pre-call checks setting, `deployment_affinity`, `session_affinity` and `responses_api_deployment_check` switch on one shared deployment-affinity filter per router [AFFINITY-001].
The name `encrypted_content_affinity`, in the setting or in a group's switches, adds the encrypted-content filter; `prompt_caching` adds the prompt-cache filter [AFFINITY-005] [AFFINITY-006].
Per-group switches set at construction, or a complexity router that uses a deployment pin, also ensure a deployment-affinity filter exists [AFFINITY-004].
The setting `enable_mid_stream_fallback_continuation` adds the continuation filter [AFFINITY-008].
Each filter takes the previous filter's output, and the encrypted-content filter runs before the deployment-affinity filter [AFFINITY-009] [AFFINITY-177].
No failure callback sees a filter's error [AFFINITY-157].

A sync router method, or an async call whose router-level strategy is not `"usage-based-routing-v2"`, `"simple-shuffle"`, `"cost-based-routing"`, `"latency-based-routing"` or `"least-busy"`, runs none of the pin filters [AFFINITY-012].

When its switches are on, the deployment-affinity filter sends a follow-up that names an earlier response back to that response's deployment, if it is still a candidate [AFFINITY-021] [AFFINITY-022] [AFFINITY-023].
Otherwise a chat session's pin decides, then the caller's pin [AFFINITY-028] [AFFINITY-029].
Order hops skip this filter's pins [AFFINITY-020].
note: Now scoped to the deployment-affinity filter, the paragraph's subject. AFFINITY-020: with a non-None `_target_order` 'the filter returns the input list unchanged without reading any pin'. It no longer conflicts with AFFINITY-056, where the encrypted-content filter still pins on an order hop.

sentence: With no usable pin, the list passes through unchanged [AFFINITY-030].
Order hops skip pins: A fallback attempt aimed at one order level gets the list back untouched, and no pin is read [AFFINITY-020].
An earlier response comes next: With response continuity on, an earlier response that names a candidate wins before the priority-group, session and caller checks [AFFINITY-022].
Priority groups skip the rest: A routing group that uses the priority strategy gets its list back unchanged [AFFINITY-024].
All candidates share one name: The pin belongs to the group name the candidates share; if they disagree, the filter steps aside [AFFINITY-025].
A session pin beats a caller pin: When session pins are active and the request has a session, a session pin that names a candidate wins [AFFINITY-028].
The caller pin comes last: With caller pins on and a known caller, a caller pin that names a candidate wins [AFFINITY-029].
note: The candidate condition is restored. AFFINITY-029: with the user-key flag on and a caller key present, 'a stored dict's `model_id` or a legacy bare-string value naming a candidate yields a one-element list'.

sentence: No usable pin changes nothing: A missing pin, or one naming no candidate, leaves the choice to the strategy [AFFINITY-030].
The caller key is the virtual key's hash from the metadata bucket, or else the user id prefixed with `user_id:` [AFFINITY-034].
The request's own user parameter never counts [AFFINITY-034].
The filter keeps a 64-character key that base-16 parsing accepts, lower-cased, and hashes any other, so raw keys and user ids never reach a cache key [AFFINITY-035].
note: Now matches AFFINITY-035's own test: 'a value exactly 64 characters long that base-16 integer parsing accepts ... is kept as-is but lower-cased'; 'any other value ... is replaced by the SHA-256 hex digest'; 'raw API keys and user ids therefore never appear in Redis keys'.

sentence: A session pin key also carries the hashed caller key, or `unscoped` without one, so two callers reusing one session id never share a pin [AFFINITY-037].
Session pins are active when the session switch is on, or when the session marker holds a positive integer [AFFINITY-026].
The filter ignores a session id that the proxy generated for a request that had none [AFFINITY-027].
A failed cache read counts as no pin [AFFINITY-032].
Just before the router sends a request to the provider, it claims the caller's and the session's pins for the chosen deployment, when those pins are switched on [AFFINITY-041] [AFFINITY-043].
The first claim wins [AFFINITY-047].
A later claim for another deployment changes nothing, while a repeat claim by the same deployment restarts the pin's lifetime, one hour by default [AFFINITY-047] [AFFINITY-003].
The writer runs inside the async call wrapper of the software development kit (SDK), under the selected deployment's own group name rather than the caller's alias [AFFINITY-041] [AFFINITY-042].
It writes nothing unless caller pins are on with a known caller, or session pins are active with a real session id [AFFINITY-043].
The lifetime is `deployment_affinity_ttl_seconds`, `3600` seconds by default; a session pin uses the session marker's value when the router set one [AFFINITY-003] [AFFINITY-046].
With Redis attached, the claim runs as one atomic Redis script [AFFINITY-048].
If that script fails, the writer claims in memory instead, which keeps the same pod sticky but loses agreement across pods [AFFINITY-049].
Errors during a claim are caught and logged at debug level, and the request goes ahead; a task cancellation still escapes [AFFINITY-051].
note: AFFINITY-051: 'an `Exception` raised during either claim ... is caught and logged at debug level', 'the request proceeds', and 'only `Exception` subclasses are caught, so `asyncio.CancelledError` propagates out of the hook'. The cancellation exception is now stated.

sentence: 0s, Caller alice: first request, no pin yet; strategy picks A
0s, Caller pin: claimed before the provider call; names A for 3600 s
10 min, Caller alice: repeat request reads the pin; served by A
10 min, Caller pin: A claims it again; expiry reset to 3600 s
20 min, Deployment A: becomes unhealthy; not a candidate
20 min, Deployment B: strategy picks B for alice; serving alice
20 min, Caller pin: B's claim loses to A; still names A
70 min, Caller pin: lifetime lapses; no pin
75 min, Deployment B: next request claims the pin; pin names B
Two overlapping first requests can land on different deployments, because reading and claiming are separate steps; the first claim wins [AFFINITY-178].
A client can send back reasoning that one deployment produced in locked form, tagged with that deployment's id [AFFINITY-058].
Only the same provider account, meaning the same address and key, keeps that reasoning [AFFINITY-069] [AFFINITY-072].
So the filter sends the request to that deployment or a twin on the same account, and otherwise removes the locked reasoning, tagged or not [AFFINITY-061] [AFFINITY-062] [AFFINITY-064].
note: AFFINITY-064's degrade path 'strips in place all litellm-marked and unmarked encrypted reasoning from `input` and all bridge-tagged blocks from messages'. In messages, every block carrying the bridge prefix is stripped whether or not it unwraps to an origin id (code: `is_encrypted_reasoning_block` tests only the `litellm_encrypted_reasoning:` prefix), so 'tagged or not' holds for both places. Natively signed blocks, which AFFINITY-067 keeps, are not account-locked reasoning in this story's sense. The routing half matches AFFINITY-061 and AFFINITY-062.

sentence: Read the origin: The filter takes the origin from the first marked input item, or else from the first tagged thinking block in the messages [AFFINITY-058] [AFFINITY-059].
Pin to the origin: If the origin is a candidate, the filter returns only it and marks the request as pinned [AFFINITY-061].
Stay on the same account: If the router still knows the origin, every candidate on the same encryption boundary is returned [AFFINITY-062].

Degrade instead of failing: Otherwise the filter logs a warning, strips the encrypted reasoning from the input and the tagged thinking blocks from the messages, and returns the candidates [AFFINITY-064] [AFFINITY-067].
The filter runs for a group when its global switch is on or the group's switches list it [AFFINITY-055].
With exactly one candidate left and the pinned mark set, the router skips the strategy, so a rate-aware strategy cannot steer the request away [AFFINITY-013].
On every fallback hop, the router repeats the strip check for the new target [AFFINITY-075].
Stripping edits the caller's lists in place, so a later attempt and an SDK caller see the stripped list [AFFINITY-068] [AFFINITY-181].
The degrade path looks the same whether the origin is cooling down, removed or forged [AFFINITY-065].
When a long prompt marks where its reusable opening ends, the router remembers which deployment served that opening [AFFINITY-101] [AFFINITY-091].
The next request with the same opening goes back to that deployment, if it is still a candidate [AFFINITY-087].
The filter leaves short prompts, and groups with a single candidate, alone [AFFINITY-082] [AFFINITY-084].
It also steps aside for a priority group, an order hop or missing chat messages [AFFINITY-080] [AFFINITY-081] [AFFINITY-083].
The pin key hashes the cacheable prefix: everything up to the last cache breakpoint, a `cache_control` marker of type `"ephemeral"` [AFFINITY-101] [AFFINITY-102].
Each block's hash chains the hash of everything before it, so a key binds the whole prefix, roles included [AFFINITY-106].
A read probes the keys of the last `20` positions, newest first, so a breakpoint that moved to a later turn still finds the deployment that cached the earlier prefix [AFFINITY-110] [AFFINITY-111].
The key comes from the messages as they will be sent, including breakpoints that auto prompt caching would inject [AFFINITY-086].
A success callback writes the pin, only for the call types `"completion"`, `"acompletion"` and `"anthropic_messages"` [AFFINITY-089].
The logged messages must reach the serving model's own cache minimum [AFFINITY-091].
A pin lasts `300` seconds, or `3600` when a breakpoint asks for `"1h"` and the deployment honours one-hour caching [AFFINITY-112] [AFFINITY-092] [AFFINITY-113].
Writes are last-writer-wins, so in a mixed group the latest serving deployment owns the prefix [AFFINITY-114].
Sometimes a streamed answer breaks after the user has already seen part of it [RCALL-008].
When continuation is switched on, the router can ask another deployment to carry on from that partial answer [AFFINITY-008] [RCALL-019] [RCALL-008].
note: Now cites the router-calls claims. RCALL-019's first condition is 'the router flag `enable_mid_stream_fallback_continuation` is on'; RCALL-008: an eligible break 'sets `messages` to the prefill continuation ... and re-enters the fallback chain'. 'Can' covers RCALL-019's further conditions, and router-calls' purpose describes such a break as 'continued on another deployment'.

sentence: Only a deployment that accepts a partial answer, and whose own settings do not reshape the output, may take over [AFFINITY-133].
The client then sees one joined reply [AFFINITY-141].
Only an eligible break puts the continuation marker on the request, and no value in request JSON can imitate it [RCALL-008] [AFFINITY-130].
Prefill support comes from the deployment's `supports_assistant_prefill` flag, or else from the model cost map [AFFINITY-131].
Constraints include more than one choice, a structured response format and a forced tool choice [AFFINITY-132].
With no deployment left, the router moves along its fallback chain and finally surfaces the original stream error [AFFINITY-133].
The splice holds the first fallback chunks while they repeat the prefill, drops a full echo, and drops re-sent trailing whitespace [AFFINITY-139] [AFFINITY-140].
With post-call rules set, the outermost splice re-checks the whole text and raises before a failing chunk reaches the client [AFFINITY-142] [AFFINITY-143].

A caller or session pin is not cleared when its deployment fails or is removed [AFFINITY-198]. Until it lapses (one hour by default) or the deployment returns, that caller's requests go elsewhere, and no other deployment can take over the pin [AFFINITY-163] [AFFINITY-003]. Only a debug-level log line records the miss [AFFINITY-030].
Caller and session pins are written before the provider answers, so a first request that fails can still pin its caller to the failing deployment [AFFINITY-041] [AFFINITY-194].

A synchronous call, and any call on a router whose routing strategy lacks an asynchronous version, skips the pin filters, and nothing is logged [AFFINITY-203]. Some of these calls still write pins that nothing reads [AFFINITY-012].

When one process builds several routers with the same filter settings, the process-wide filter list keeps only the first router's filters, so every router uses that router's pin stores [AFFINITY-200] [AFFINITY-202]. Discarding that first router silently turns the filters off for the rest [AFFINITY-202].

A reasoning tag carries no signature, so a client can steer a request to any candidate it names [AFFINITY-154]. They do not check caller or session identity either; they rely on the proxy's authentication step, or the calling program, to fill it in truthfully [AFFINITY-184].
When reasoning cannot return to its origin, the follow-up turn loses it with no error; only a log warning shows it [AFFINITY-159].
Near the prompt-cache size limit, the read check and the write check measure against different models, so some pins are written but never read [AFFINITY-199].

When the encrypted-content filter leaves a single pinned deployment, the request skips the routing strategy [AFFINITY-013]. Under usage-based routing version 2, a pinned deployment already at its requests-per-minute limit then fails the request with a rate-limit error to the caller, and goes into cooldown [AFFINITY-013].
